why: The jumps only go right, so this is the classic 'max score path to the last index' 1-D DP: dp[i] = arr[i] + max(dp[i-1], dp[i-p]) over the allowed jump lengths p. The maths part is sieving the primes that end in 3.
hints: You must land exactly on the last index, and each landing adds its value, including negative ones.
The legal jumps are 1 and primes p with p % 10 == 3 (3, 13, 23, 43, 53, 73, 83, 103, ...). Sieve once up to n.
dp[0] = arr[0]. For each i, take the best of dp[i-1] and dp[i-p] for listed primes p <= i, then add arr[i]. Answer dp[n-1]. O(n * P), where P is the number of such primes.
pitfalls: 33, 63 and 93 end in 3 but are not prime.
Values can be negative, so start the max at -infinity or dp[i-1], not 0.
